subject: Capacity smoothing proposal & multi-year term curve — Orbis AI
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@orbis.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@orbis.ai; diego@orbis.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask: smoothing multi-year commit and term discounts

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood Dedicated. Before we ask procurement to draw up paperwork, we need a clearer picture on pricing mechanics for a multi-year prepay. High-level ask: can you provide a proposal that smooths capacity across quarters/year while preserving progressive term discounts?

Context:
- Orbis projects bursty usage (model experimentation Q1/Q2, steady serving Q3–Q4).
- We want to commit to a 3-year reserved pool but avoid heavy overcommit in year 1.
- Key asks: inter-quarter smoothing (ability to shift commit between quarters), a clear discount curve for 1/2/3-year terms, and a path to increase capacity mid-term without punitive repricing.

Can you share options (a conservative offer and a smoothing-friendly offer) and any constraints around carry-forward credits or buy-downs?

Procurement will need a compact order summary (numbers by GPU/TM, annual spend, and any early-exit clauses).

Thanks — copying Diego and our procurement alias.

— Emma
Head of Infrastructure, Orbis AI

From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@orbis.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask: smoothing multi-year commit and term discounts

Emma — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching a first-pass proposal (Redwood_Dedicated_Capacity_Smoothing_Proposal_v1.pdf) and a short explainer below.

Summary (two options):
1) Conservative Multi-year (low flexibility)
   - Year 1: 40% of target TPU/GPU committed, Year 2: 70%, Year 3: 100%
   - Discounts: 1yr = 8%, 2yr = 12%, 3yr = 18% off list for dedicated capacity
   - Limited smoothing: ability to shift up to 10% between quarters; unused commit converts to one-time credits at 50% value

2) Smoothing-friendly (higher flexibility)
   - Blended commit curve with smoothing buffer: Year 1: 55%, Year 2: 75%, Year 3: 100%
   - Discounts: 1yr = 10%, 2yr = 14%, 3yr = 20%
   - Shift allowance: up to 25% inter-quarter shift; excess use billed at on-demand rates; unused prepay carries forward as credit for next 6 months

Other items:
- Mid-term scale-up: add capacity at the then-current list price; we offer a 6% step-up discount on incremental capacity added within the same contract year.
- SLA / credits: standard Dedicated SLA with token-level latency targets; we can add tighter SLOs to contract for a reciprocal credit table (finance to confirm).

Next steps:
- Monica and I will build a clean order summary for procurement.
- Can we schedule a 30-minute call next Tuesday to align on which option you prefer and any mandatory procurement terms?

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_Dedicated_Capacity_Smoothing_Proposal_v1.pdf
From: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@orbis.ai>; dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Jul 2026 14:21:00 -0700
Subject: Orbis — order summary and operational guardrails

Emma — following up with numbers you requested. I pulled a short order summary and a proposed mutual action plan (attached Order_Summary_OrbisAI_v2.xlsx). Highlights below.

Proposed baseline (example) — Dedicated GPUs (NVIDIA A100-equivalent)
- Baseline pool target: 100 units (target for year 3)
- Offer A (smoothing-friendly): Year1 commit 55 units (55%), Year2 75 units (75%), Year3 100 units (100%)
- Blended pricing (list $/GPU-hour): base $X; effective discounts yield blended rates of $Y (Y in spreadsheet)

Operational guardrails (to reduce billing friction):
- Inter-quarter smoothing cap: 25% of quarterly baseline (up/down)
- Carry-forward credit: unused prepay converts to monthly credits redeemable for 6 months
- Overuse: billed at 1.5x the committed unit rate (not full on-demand) — helps caps runaway spend while preserving predictability
- Mid-term decrease: allowed once per year with a 90-day notice; buy-down compensates Redwood at 40% of remaining prepaid value

Mutual action plan (MAP):
- This week: Agree on smoothing cap and preferred discount curve (you)
- Next week: Redwood to deliver term sheet and order summary (we)
- Week +2: Orbis legal to send redlines, finance to confirm PO cadence

Attachment: Order_Summary_OrbisAI_v2.xlsx

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Senior Sales Operations Manager — Redwood Inference
From: Emma Liu <emma@orbis.ai>
To: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurements@orbis.ai; diego@orbis.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orbis — order summary and operational guardrails

Thanks Monica — the numbers are helpful. A few clarifying points from procurement and legal:

1) Smoothing cap: procurement can accept up to 30% inter-quarter smoothing (higher than your 25%) if there is a symmetrical buyout / floor protection for Redwood in the event we materially under-utilize the committed pool.
2) Buy-down / exit: we want a capped buyout for year 2 if usage < 50% of that year's commit — proposal: allow buyout with 20% of remaining prepaid value retained by Redwood.
3) Credits: carry-forward credits are good, but we need clear visibility (reporting hooks) and trigger events for credit expiry.
4) SLA escalation: can you add a clause for accelerated remediation (1 business day response + 48-hour mitigation plan) for incidents that affect >10% of our requests?

I've attached a draft SOW with these asks (Orbis_SOW_draft.docx). Please review and flag any impossible asks. If we can align on smoothing cap and buyout mechanics, procurement says they're comfortable moving to PO.

— Emma
From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma@orbis.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Orbis — order summary and operational guardrails (proposed compromise)

Emma — appreciate the clear redlines. High level response below; finance and legal are reviewing the SOW and we can bake the final language into the term sheet. Attached: term-sheet-orbis-v3.pdf with the compromise terms.

Compromise (proposed):
- Inter-quarter smoothing: allow up to 25% by default, with a one-time election to expand to 30% on contract signing (requires a proportional premium of +1.5% on blended rate).
- Buyout / year2 under-utilization: if year2 usage < 50% of year2 commit, Orbis may buy out the remaining prepay balance; Redwood retains 25% of remaining prepaid value (split of your 20% ask and our 40% initial ask).
- Credits & reporting: we will expose a 'prepay ledger' in the Redwood Console (monthly statements) and credits expire after 6 months; we will provide a sync report during monthly business reviews.
- SLA escalation: agree to accelerated remediation clause (1 business day response + 48-hour mitigation plan) for incidents impacting >10% traffic; legal to formalize the credit table.

Pricing curve (example final):
- Year1: 12% discount on list for committed capacity
- Year2: 16% discount
- Year3: 20% discount

Next steps:
1) Monica to finalize a concise order summary tying the term-sheet numbers to PO lines.
2) Legal / finance will incorporate the buyout and smoothing election language into the SPA; I will share the updated term sheet by EOD tomorrow.
3) If Orbis is comfortable, we can provision initial Year1 capacity within 30 days of contract signature.

Links: proposal (https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/ORBS-042/proposal), HubSpot record HS-10023.

Thanks — look forward to getting this over the line.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachment: term-sheet-orbis-v3.pdf
